analysis:
The change is a documentation-only edit to docs/architecture/inference.md, and only the base-side text excerpts (lines 2839-3590) were supplied. The changed hunks are in the patch: the date bump, the KV re-slice floor paragraph near line 985, a new cluster-service health-file paragraph inserted at head 3532-3540, and later hunks around 5234+ that were not visible in these units. No executable code, cryptographic logic, or authorization logic changes in the visible evidence.

Security-relevant observations:
- The new heartbeat/health-file paragraph (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE, service-health.json versus part-health.json) describes supervisor liveness accepting only a beat with the service's own PID. This touches TB-003 (operator versus process) and the availability of cluster members. It is documentation of an env-var-driven path, and the implementation (ClusterServiceAgent.healthPath, ClusterService.partEnvironment) was not supplied. Whether the health file lives in an owner-only directory and whether the PID check is robust against a same-UID writer is unverified. It is a possible T-043/T-059-style local DoS surface, but it is not evidence of a regression.
- The KV re-slice floor paragraph (head 985-989) describes funding workspace-aware floors first. It touches availability and memory admission (T-016/T-029 class) and is a design statement only.
- The base excerpts cover cluster lanes, the Flint constraints, and the link-probe history file (~/.darkbloom/cluster/link-probes.json, described as owner-only). They are unchanged context, and no new weakening of the prefix-cache threat T-041, of A-001 plaintext handling, or of coordinator trust is introduced.

The remaining hunks (head 5234-5298, 5374-5376) were not visible, so the analysis of them is incomplete. Integration should confirm that the actual code behind the health-file change creates the file with owner-only permissions and does not follow symlinks. No findings.
